title: Charcoal burner
description:
The location of a charcoal burners' site (a site, often in a woodland clearing, used for the production of pure carbon by the controlled burning of wood and other organic materials) of Modern date.

Located next to a forestry trackway, the burner was a large cast iron cylinder (2m in diameter) with a lid and four air inlet pipes. Surrounding the burner was a log pile comprising burnt and unburnt wood and a large pile of charcoal. This site was located during a field survey conducted by LUAU in 1999 (S1896).

title: Gelli Rhyd charcoal mounds
description: A number of charcoal mounds averaging 8m across and surviving as circular platforms on hillslope terraces with charcoal makeup.  Documentary evidence indicates charcoal burning was widespread in this area during the 17th and 18th centuries. The charcoal was used for iron blast furnaces in Blaenavon and at Glangrwyney (not previously known to SMR).

title: Charcoal Pitsteads, Loughrigg Fell
description:
A charcoal burners' site (a site, often in a woodland clearing, used for the production of pure carbon by the controlled burning of wood and other organic materials) of unknown date. See also HERs 30674-30677.

Numerous charcoal pitsteads within the area, including HERs 30674-30677. This site is included on M Davies Shiel's annotated map 1990 (S1286). Charcoal burning platforms recorded in The National Trust Sites and Monuments Record. The locations of individual pitsteads, where recorded, has been detailed by The Trust. The site also includes a number of unassigned earthwork platforms, which are likely to be further charcoal burning platforms. It is thought that these remains are Post Medieval in date (S2873). There is one revetted level platform, which looks initially like a pitstead but has one straight edge (revetment) and faint outline of rectangular building (possibly as a charcoal store or accommodation?). The charcoal burning platforms are slight earthworks and have been revetted on downslope sides. Dimensions of the individual charcoal burning platforms vary (S3086).

title: Porterthwaite Charcoal Burning Platforms
description:
Site of a charcoal burning platform (an area of flattened or compacted ground used for charcoal burning) of Post Medieval date. See associated HER 32223.

A scatter of seven charcoal burning platforms within Porterthwaite coppice and possibly associated with a charcoal burners hut (SMR 32223). The majority of the platforms are between 6m and 8m in diameter, and have been cut into the hillside to form a level circular platform on the down slope side. Two at NY 14060 01030 and NY 14020 01010 are 'banana' shaped. This site was surveyed by LUAU in 2000 (S1892).

title: Undated charcoal burners sites
description:
Several charcoal burners sites of unknown date which were used for making pure carbon. They are situated 100m west of Daniels Wood.

{1} Large circular areas of dark organic soil 9m in diameter. Two of these patches occurring within the motorway corridor were sectioned and in both cases natural marl occurred at depth of 25 cm below the surface. The dark colour was due to a considerable amount of charcoal which had been distributed evenly throughout the soil by ploughing. No trace of structures or of pottery was found. These are presumably traces of charcoal-burning.
